<edits>
No component changes. All six candidates (inv1-3, dom1-3) display "harness.diff: (no change)" and are identical to base_harness in every component: harness.py, prompts/system.md, prompts/task.md. The three aggregation candidates (agg1-3) are also code-identical to base. Variation among the three agg deliverables arose entirely from LLM output formatting choices (agg1: "Final Balance:" with capital B; agg2: "Final balance:" with lowercase b; agg3: "Final balance: $..." with unrequested currency symbol). The LLM, not the harness, introduced these differences. All three harnesses executed identically and all three delivered the numerically correct answer: 2,366,974.
</edits>

<experience>
cue: A deterministic computational task where all base rollouts converge on an identical, correct answer with zero divergence, and a library pattern (code extraction mechanism + explicit code-generation instruction) exists for structurally similar tasks but is documented as applicable only when base runs produce divergent outputs.

lesson: In harness.py and prompts/task.md, do not add code extraction mechanism or explicit code-generation instruction to deterministic arithmetic tasks that already demonstrate base convergence and correct execution. The proven pattern from holdout-numeric-002, 003, 005, 010 is transferable to tasks exhibiting base divergence; applying it to already-converged harnesses speculates beyond evidence and increases token cost with no observed benefit.

evidence: All six independent decision blocks (inv1, inv2, inv3, dom1, dom2, dom3) reached KEEP_BASE independently. Each observed: (a) zero divergence in base1, base2, base3 (all returned 2,366,974); (b) library pattern cues explicitly document divergence as the trigger condition (e.g., holdout-numeric-003 cue: "unaided LLM reasoning diverges across runs... producing divergent results"); (c) no trajectory moment showed failure, error, or omission. All six cited mission guidance: "Do not fix what the runs already got right" and "Every edit must trace to a moment in a trajectory; if you cannot name the moment, the edit is speculation and costs context for nothing." The adoption of agg2 over agg1/agg3 was based on output formatting preference (plainest form), not harness improvement—all three harnesses were code-identical and all runs succeeded.

confidence: high. The record explicitly documents: nine rollouts (three base + six candidates), all with identical harness code, all producing correct answer, zero divergence. The library pattern's documented prerequisite (base divergence) is absent. Six independent reviewers reached the same conclusion through the same logic. Mission guidance explicitly forbids speculative additions to working solutions. No trajectory moment supports applying the pattern.
</experience>
